story.iWant: to see a photo-realistic 3D marble cube that responds to my configuration in real-time
story.soThat: I can visualize exactly what my custom marble cube will look like and feel confident in my purchase decision

tasks.task: Create CubeViewer component with React Three Fiber 1.1: Create src/components/3d/CubeViewer.tsx with Canvas setup 1.2: Configure Canvas with frameloop="demand" for performance 1.3: Set scene background to #0D0D0D (Nero Marquina) 1.4: Wrap with Suspense and provide loading fallback 1.5: Accept width, height, depth props from store 1.6: Create MarbleCube mesh with BoxGeometry using store dimensions

Implement marble texture loading 2.1: Create src/components/3d/MarbleMaterial.tsx for PBR material 2.2: Use Drei useTexture hook for loading diffuse, normal, roughness maps 2.3: Configure texture paths dynamically based on marbleSlug 2.4: Implement texture tiling/repeat based on cube dimensions 2.5: Add texture loading error handling with fallback 2.6: Implement texture crossfade on marble change (optional)

Implement finish-based material properties 3.1: Create roughness value mapping: POLISHED(0.1), HONED(0.5), RAW(0.9), BRUSHED(0.7) 3.2: Apply roughness to MeshStandardMaterial based on store finish 3.3: Adjust metalness and envMapIntensity per finish type 3.4: Test all four finish types visually

Configure studio lighting environment 4.1: Create src/components/3d/SceneLighting.tsx for lights setup 4.2: Use Drei Environment component with "studio" preset 4.3: Add ambient light for base fill (low intensity) 4.4: Add directional key light for shadows 4.5: Fine-tune lighting for "private atelier" aesthetic

Implement contact shadow 5.1: Use Drei ContactShadow component beneath cube 5.2: Configure shadow opacity, blur, and scale 5.3: Position shadow to scale with cube dimensions 5.4: Match shadow color to Nero Marquina theme

Connect to Zustand configuration store 6.1: Import selectors from configStore (useMarbleSlug, useWidth, etc.) 6.2: Subscribe CubeViewer to relevant state changes 6.3: Trigger re-render on dimension, marble, or finish changes 6.4: Verify reactivity - changes update 3D view in real-time

Integrate with ThreeDViewport 7.1: Update ThreeDViewport.tsx to render CubeViewer instead of placeholder 7.2: Pass necessary props from store to CubeViewer 7.3: Maintain Suspense loading state during texture load 7.4: Test responsive behavior at desktop and mobile breakpoints

Performance optimization 8.1: Implement frameloop="demand" to render only on changes 8.2: Use useFrame invalidation for smooth updates 8.3: Profile initial load time (target < 3s) 8.4: Profile frame rate during interaction (target 60fps) 8.5: Add texture compression notes for production optimization

Testing and verification 9.1: Visual test with each marble type (10 marbles) 9.2: Visual test with each finish type (4 finishes) 9.3: Test dimension changes (min 5cm, max 100cm, various sizes) 9.4: Test on desktop (1440px) and mobile (375px) 9.5: Verify TypeScript compiles with no errors 9.6: Verify build succeeds (npm run build)

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: 3D cube renders with accurate dimensions from configuration store - Cube geometry updates when width, height, or depth change - Dimensions displayed in real-world scale (1 unit = 1 cm) - Cube remains centered in viewport regardless of dimensions - Dimension changes reflect within 500ms (NFR3)

Photo-realistic marble textures with proper PBR materials - Diffuse texture (color/pattern) loads from /public/textures/{marble-slug}/diffuse.png - Normal map loads from /public/textures/{marble-slug}/normal.png - Roughness map loads from /public/textures/{marble-slug}/roughness.png - Textures tile appropriately based on cube scale - Texture swapping when marble type changes is smooth (crossfade effect)

Finish affects material properties visually - POLISHED: Low roughness (0.1), high reflectivity, mirror-like - HONED: Medium roughness (0.5), matte appearance, no sharp reflections - RAW: High roughness (0.9), natural stone texture prominent - BRUSHED: Medium-high roughness (0.7), anisotropic appearance - Finish changes reflect immediately in 3D view

Realistic studio lighting environment - HDRI environment map for realistic reflections (studio preset) - Ambient light for base illumination - Key light for primary shadows and highlights - Lighting consistent with "private atelier" aesthetic

Subtle shadow beneath the cube - Contact shadow or ground plane shadow visible - Shadow size scales proportionally with cube dimensions - Shadow soft and realistic (not hard-edged) - Shadow color blends with Nero Marquina background
Scene background matches Nero Marquina theme - Canvas background: #0D0D0D - No distracting elements in scene - Cube is the clear focal point

Performance targets met - Initial 3D load < 3 seconds on broadband connection (NFR1) - Rendering at 60fps during idle (NFR2) - Texture loading with Suspense (loading state shown) - frameloop="demand" for battery/CPU efficiency when idle

Integration with existing ThreeDViewport placeholder - Replaces loading shimmer with actual 3D canvas - Maintains responsive sizing from Story 3.1 layout - Works in both desktop (70% viewport) and mobile (60% viewport) layouts

docs.doc: Declarative Three.js rendering, useTexture for marble texture loading with Suspense, OrbitControls for camera manipulation, Environment for realistic lighting (studio HDRI), useFrame for animation loop when needed.
Texture compression (WebP/AVIF for previews, JPG for 3D), progressive texture loading, geometry instancing, requestAnimationFrame throttling on idle, dynamic import with ssr: false.
FR17: 3D renders photo-realistic marble textures with accurate veining. FR18: All configurator changes update 3D view in real-time (< 500ms).
NFR1: 3D configurator initial load < 3s. NFR2: Configurator interactions at 60fps. NFR3: Changes reflect within 500ms. NFR6: Performance acceptable on mid-range mobile (2020+).
Background: Rich Black #0D0D0D, Surface: Dark Gray #1A1A1A, Border: Medium Gray #2D2D2D, Accent: Champagne Gold #C9A962, Text: Pure White #FFFFFF.
Cube3DViewer: Three.js viewport with rotation, zoom, lighting. Key states: Loading, Ready, Error.
Full story definition with acceptance criteria in BDD format, prerequisites: Story 3.1, 3.2, 2.2.

constraints.constraint: React Three Fiber components must use dynamic import with ssr: false to prevent server-side rendering issues
Use Drei useTexture hook within Suspense boundary for texture loading
Use individual Zustand selectors (useMarbleSlug, useWidth, etc.) to minimize re-renders
Follow naming convention: PascalCase for components (CubeViewer.tsx, MarbleMaterial.tsx)
Visual testing only for 3D - no unit tests required for WebGL components
Add aria-label describing configuration for screen readers per UX spec 8.2
Use frameloop="demand" to only render when state changes
Textures are PNG format (not JPG) - update texture paths accordingly
